scope: Frozen invented-object prototype only; no TX graph, incomplete pickle, compile, sampler, or owner files touched

independent_run.method: Copied only counting.py and test_counting.py into a fresh /tmp directory; ran nice -n 15 python3 -B test_counting.py with bytecode disabled.
independent_run.result: all eight invented-object tests passed in 3.671 seconds
independent_run.artifacts: Created only in the disposable /tmp copy's new UUID test fixture; no packet outputs overwritten.

supported: The sink checks the next write budget before accepting/hash accumulation, hashes accepted data in bounded 64 KiB slices and reports accepted-prefix counters. Tiny complete fixture length and digest agree with independent pickle.dumps bytes.

Completion is published only after child exit code zero, current source/request checks, candidate checks and file pinning. Death after candidate, logical-budget failure and tested CPU signal leave no completion marker. Verification checks an externally supplied complete-manifest hash and all listed files with path/symlink checks.

No serialized payload is persisted and the prototype explicitly disallows deserialization. Source/request expectations are caller-selected local byte identities, not independent authorization. It only tests invented data, not graph serialization demand or restoration.

gaps_and_corrections.finding: The source labels SIGXCPU termination `hard_cpu_soft_limit_signal`, although RLIMIT_CPU soft is 2 CPU seconds and hard is 3. The findings narrative correctly explains it is the soft-limit signal; rename the terminal reason to avoid misleading evidence.

The controller has no try/finally cleanup around the live child if the controller is interrupted or an exception occurs after Popen (for example, while writing launch.json). Such a controller failure can leave the toy child running and no terminal receipt. Watchdog-triggered cleanup is tested, but controller death/exception cleanup is not. Before real use, arrange bounded process-group cleanup and preserve an explicit incomplete terminal state.

If progress atomic_json itself fails after sink bytes were counted in memory, the latest accepted-prefix counter may not be durably recorded; no completion is produced, but failure.json does not include the sink snapshot. The claimed prefix is therefore only the latest successfully persisted progress record.

Progress is fsynced on every Pickler write: each callback causes temp-file create/write/fsync, rename and directory fsync. This is correct for the tiny crash tests but potentially expensive; measure and specify any checkpoint-throttled lower-bound contract before a larger sink run.

The complete-manifest verifier proves byte identity under trusted local generation, not authorization. Preserve the explicit `deserialization_authorized=false` boundary. Any future pickle restore must require authenticated locally generated completed bytes and a separate safe restore test; hashes alone do not make untrusted pickle safe.

resource_limits: Tested CPU termination and effective limits on toy child; address-space/file exhaustion were not exercised. RSS/output/wall are polling watchdogs (50 ms), so can overshoot. No actual-graph memory, output, timing or disk demand is evidenced.
recommendation: Accept only as a successful small invented-object sink prototype. Fix terminal reason and controller cleanup gaps before adapting to a new, separately reviewed bounded experiment. Do not infer actual graph feasibility or restore safety.
